set.reason: The modeled rational equation must be solved and its candidates checked against denominator exclusions and the context.
set.scope: solving and checking the modeled rational equation

set.reason: Division applications prepare inverse unit-rate questions. The actual forward criteria multiply price by quantity and speed by time, without solving a division story or checking a remainder.
set.scope: inverse quantity relations solved by division

set.reason: The earlier application endpoint explicitly distinguishes each-group amount from group count. Those meanings underlie the unit-price-times-quantity abstraction, as Gemini observes. Restrict this edge to that conceptual component rather than requiring two-digit arithmetic or a previously completed application lesson.
set.scope: Per-unit amount and number-of-groups meanings in total-price and speed-times-time relationships

set.reason: The endpoint provides explicit quantity-modeling experience that can help translate a fraction-of-a-whole story into an expression. Price and speed formulas do not define a fractional part, so the benefit is preparation only. This final scoped judgment does not treat a prior native acceptance of Claude's rejection as an accepted dependency.
set.scope: Prior experience representing total, part and multiplicative relationships in application problems

set.reason: The unit-whole criterion interprets a fractional part of the whole and then inverts that relation. Fraction-of-a-quantity modeling is necessary, without requiring the endpoint's preferred arithmetic implementation.
set.scope: identifying the unit whole in the fraction relation
